stem:
Meena connects the same nichrome wire first to one cell and then to two cells, each time for exactly 5 minutes, and compares the heat produced. Her brother says the heating of wires is always a bad thing.
Which statement is correct?

options.text: Two cells produce more heat in the same time, but all electrical heating is harmful, including in an electric iron.
Two cells produce more heat in the same time than one cell, and this heating is useful in appliances like an iron but harmful when a plug overheats.
One cell produces more heat than two cells in the same wire over the same time, and this heating is useful in an electric iron.
The same wire produces the same heat with one cell or two cells in 5 minutes, so overheating at a plug cannot happen.

teacher.key_rationale: For the same wire and duration, more cells drive more current and so more heat; heating is useful in appliances (iron, heater) but unwanted overheating damages plugs and sockets. Only B states both correctly. A reverses the useful/harmful judgement, C reverses the cell comparison, D denies both the comparison and the hazard.
